Round your answer to $2$ decimal places." :question/worked-solution "By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required probability is given by

$$
P(Y=3\,|\,X=2)=\frac{P(X=2,Y=3)}{P(X=2)}=\frac{f(2,3)}{{f}_{X}(2)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(2) & =0.05+0.25 \\  & =0.30\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(2,3)=0.25.$ 

Finally, substituting ${f}_{X}(2)=0.30$ and $f(2,3)=0.25$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=3\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{f(2,3)}{{f}_{X}(2)} \\  & =\frac{0.25}{0.30} \\  & ≈0.83.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186159434 :answer-field/correct 17592186159436 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "question-dd1f8e38-c35e-55be-bdf0-b84dac107dde" :question/id #uuid "dd1f8e38-c35e-55be-bdf0-b84dac107dde" :question/math-academy-id "q-142884" :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |

Compute $P(Y=0\,|\,X=3)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above." :question/worked-solution "By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required probability is given by

$$
P(Y=0\,|\,X=3)=\frac{P(X=3,Y=0)}{P(X=3)}=\frac{f(3,0)}{{f}_{X}(3)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(3) & =f(3,0)+f(3,1)+f(3,2) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{2}{18}+\frac{2}{18}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{5}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(3,0)=\frac{1}{9}.$ 

Finally, substituting ${f}_{X}(3)=\frac{5}{18}$ and $f(3,0)=\frac{1}{9}$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=0\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{f(3,0)}{{f}_{X}(3)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{9})}{(\frac{5}{18})} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-267ccec5-8a84-5cdf-a568-00ac33d5a7c7"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-267ccec5-8a84-5cdf-a568-00ac33d5a7c7" :answer-field/id #uuid "267ccec5-8a84-5cdf-a568-00ac33d5a7c7" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-f9b91a68-f1a7-5800-9852-2b8c8adc0a07" :answer-field/choices ["answer-7df7cc62-41f2-5b67-8003-b3f2f792fe42" "answer-dd26a283-a544-5be7-b680-07b8f95e6c0e" "answer-cece1cdf-fe31-5b7b-9e6c-984391d3198f" "answer-9258e615-4af2-514e-a284-343d0ce33226" "answer-f9b91a68-f1a7-5800-9852-2b8c8adc0a07"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7df7cc62-41f2-5b67-8003-b3f2f792fe42" :answer/id #uuid "7df7cc62-41f2-5b67-8003-b3f2f792fe42" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-dd26a283-a544-5be7-b680-07b8f95e6c0e" :answer/id #uuid "dd26a283-a544-5be7-b680-07b8f95e6c0e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cece1cdf-fe31-5b7b-9e6c-984391d3198f" :answer/id #uuid "cece1cdf-fe31-5b7b-9e6c-984391d3198f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9258e615-4af2-514e-a284-343d0ce33226" :answer/id #uuid "9258e615-4af2-514e-a284-343d0ce33226" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{2}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f9b91a68-f1a7-5800-9852-2b8c8adc0a07" :answer/id #uuid "f9b91a68-f1a7-5800-9852-2b8c8adc0a07" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{2}{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-5f05ade6-f4a6-518d-b188-3b387ae00a2d" :question/id #uuid "5f05ade6-f4a6-518d-b188-3b387ae00a2d" :question/math-academy-id "q-142862" :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ | $Y=7$ |

| $X=0$ | $0.05$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ |

Compute $P(1<Y<7\,|\,X=2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above." :question/worked-solution "By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<Y<7\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{P((1<Y<7),X=2)}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=2,(1<Y<7))}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=2,Y=3)+P(X=2,Y=5)}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{f(2,3)+f(2,5)}{{f}_{X}(2)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(2) & =f(2,1)+f(2,3)+f(2,5)+f(2,7) \\  & =0+0.05+0.05+0.1 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(2,3)=0.05$ and $f(2,5)=0.05.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<Y<7\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{f(2,3)+f(2,5)}{{f}_{X}(2)} \\  & =\frac{0.05+0.05}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.1}{0.2} \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-28ba60db-712f-5d88-8bab-1c42ece049bb"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-28ba60db-712f-5d88-8bab-1c42ece049bb" :answer-field/id #uuid "28ba60db-712f-5d88-8bab-1c42ece049bb" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-cfc7ea99-dc34-5c5e-b665-c3586432a818" :answer-field/choices ["answer-5da297a0-8c40-5743-92dd-89674c59b084" "answer-778478e6-34f7-5241-9c21-a6104ba3033d" "answer-558ce6b2-7ed9-580c-a0dc-2f742abaac0a" "answer-cfc7ea99-dc34-5c5e-b665-c3586432a818" "answer-b8532e0e-af6a-5a33-b916-4185a356c949"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5da297a0-8c40-5743-92dd-89674c59b084" :answer/id #uuid "5da297a0-8c40-5743-92dd-89674c59b084" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-778478e6-34f7-5241-9c21-a6104ba3033d" :answer/id #uuid "778478e6-34f7-5241-9c21-a6104ba3033d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.25" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-558ce6b2-7ed9-580c-a0dc-2f742abaac0a" :answer/id #uuid "558ce6b2-7ed9-580c-a0dc-2f742abaac0a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cfc7ea99-dc34-5c5e-b665-c3586432a818" :answer/id #uuid "cfc7ea99-dc34-5c5e-b665-c3586432a818" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.5" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b8532e0e-af6a-5a33-b916-4185a356c949" :answer/id #uuid "b8532e0e-af6a-5a33-b916-4185a356c949" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.75" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-29c9824b-2b87-54bb-a940-69ce3efe0d1b" :question/id #uuid "29c9824b-2b87-54bb-a940-69ce3efe0d1b" :question/math-academy-id "q-142904" :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |

Compute $P(0\le X<2\,|\,Y=4)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above." :question/worked-solution "By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X<2\,|\,Y=4) & =\frac{P((0\le X<2),Y=4)}{P(Y=4)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=0,Y=4)+P(X=1,Y=4)}{P(Y=4)} \\  & =\frac{f(0,4)+f(1,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(4) & =f(0,4)+f(1,4)+f(2,4) \\  & =0.05+0.1+0.05 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(0,4)=0.05$ and $f(1,4)=0.1.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X<2\,|\,Y=4) & =\frac{f(0,4)+f(1,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)} \\  & =\frac{0.05+0.1}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.15}{0.2} \\  & =0.75.\end{aligned}

Find the conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)$ given that the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above." :question/worked-solution "The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the following set of conditional probabilities:

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=2)
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X=x\,|\,Y=2)=\frac{P(X=x,Y=2)}{P(Y=2)}=\frac{f(x,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.6$ | $0.4$ | $1$ |

Therefore, for $x\in \{0,2,4\},$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,|\,Y=2) & =\frac{f(0,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}=\frac{0.1}{0.4}=\frac{1}{4} \\ P(X=2\,|\,Y=2) & =\frac{f(2,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}=\frac{0.2}{0.4}=\frac{1}{2} \\ P(X=4\,|\,Y=2) & =\frac{f(4,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}=\frac{0.1}{0.4}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the conditional probability mass function can be represented by the following table:   

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-295a6c8e-d0f1-5ddc-b043-2d9d231b86a4"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-295a6c8e-d0f1-5ddc-b043-2d9d231b86a4" :answer-field/id #uuid "295a6c8e-d0f1-5ddc-b043-2d9d231b86a4" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-b4efca0f-c1ba-5117-b9f7-7813f9a55b58" :answer-field/choices ["answer-06f6b37e-e1c4-56fe-af0d-d05220252493" "answer-b4efca0f-c1ba-5117-b9f7-7813f9a55b58" "answer-b80e5bda-3113-58c2-972b-15fe4ed4a1f9" "answer-4329cac3-a508-561d-92e3-75791b4b2a53" "answer-6429f8f1-6f22-5c87-b7fa-2aa976d2cf28"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-06f6b37e-e1c4-56fe-af0d-d05220252493" :answer/id #uuid "06f6b37e-e1c4-56fe-af0d-d05220252493" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |

$$
P(Y=y\,|\,X=2)=\frac{P(X=2,Y=y)}{P(X=2)}=\frac{f(2,y)}{{f}_{X}(2)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

where ![](images/fd/fdb49440ceb7e11cd9ba0b0869a1e6d3565549969180830d1796db7dd00a2b96.svg) is the marginal mass function of ![](images/ed/ed6dc1fd057e3dd2207c735a562bf4db22b72d1a9380651607439f00c0440725.svg) This formula assumes that ![](images/f8/f8020df80e303daf760cd9bf4d8437cc08bc4b95b0ccf64bc7a43ccddc650f5f.svg)" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186163325 :tutorial/content "We can now define two more probability mass functions as follows:

- The **conditional probability mass function of $X$ given that $Y=y$,** denoted $f_{X|Y}(x|y),$ is defined as

$$
f_{X|Y}(x|y) = P(X = x \,|\, Y = y) = \dfrac{P(X = x, \, Y = y)}{P(Y=y)} = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y(y)},
$$

where  $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal mass function of $Y.$

- The **conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x,$** denoted $f_{Y|X}(y|x),$ is defined as

$$
f_{Y|X}(y|x) = P(Y = y \,|\, X = x) = \dfrac{P(X = x,\, Y = y)}{P(X=x)} = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)},
$$

where  $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal mass function of $X.$

**Watch out!** The conditional distribution of $X$ given $Y$ does *not* equal the conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$. That is, in general,

$$
f_{X|Y}(x|y)  \ne f_{Y|X}(y|x).
$$

Finally, if $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then 

$$
f_{X|Y}(x|y)=f_X(x),\qquad f_{Y|X}(y|x)=f_Y(y).
$$

In other words, if $X$  and  $Y$ are independent, then knowing the value of one random variable does not affect the probability distribution of the other." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186162164 :activity/expected-seconds 660.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

$$
P(Y=0\,|\,X=3)=\frac{P(X=3,Y=0)}{P(X=3)}=\frac{f(3,0)}{{f}_{X}(3)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(3) & =f(3,0)+f(3,1)+f(3,2) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{2}{18}+\frac{2}{18}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{5}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

Compute $P(1<Y<7\,|\,X=2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above." :question/worked-solution "By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<Y<7\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{P((1<Y<7),X=2)}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=2,(1<Y<7))}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=2,Y=3)+P(X=2,Y=5)}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{f(2,3)+f(2,5)}{{f}_{X}(2)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(2) & =f(2,1)+f(2,3)+f(2,5)+f(2,7) \\  & =0+0.05+0.05+0.1 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(2,3)=0.05$ and $f(2,5)=0.05.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<Y<7\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{f(2,3)+f(2,5)}{{f}_{X}(2)} \\  & =\frac{0.05+0.05}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.1}{0.2} \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-28ba60db-712f-5d88-8bab-1c42ece049bb"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-28ba60db-712f-5d88-8bab-1c42ece049bb" :answer-field/id #uuid "28ba60db-712f-5d88-8bab-1c42ece049bb" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-cfc7ea99-dc34-5c5e-b665-c3586432a818" :answer-field/choices ["answer-5da297a0-8c40-5743-92dd-89674c59b084" "answer-778478e6-34f7-5241-9c21-a6104ba3033d" "answer-558ce6b2-7ed9-580c-a0dc-2f742abaac0a" "answer-cfc7ea99-dc34-5c5e-b665-c3586432a818" "answer-b8532e0e-af6a-5a33-b916-4185a356c949"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5da297a0-8c40-5743-92dd-89674c59b084" :answer/id #uuid "5da297a0-8c40-5743-92dd-89674c59b084" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-778478e6-34f7-5241-9c21-a6104ba3033d" :answer/id #uuid "778478e6-34f7-5241-9c21-a6104ba3033d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.25" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-558ce6b2-7ed9-580c-a0dc-2f742abaac0a" :answer/id #uuid "558ce6b2-7ed9-580c-a0dc-2f742abaac0a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cfc7ea99-dc34-5c5e-b665-c3586432a818" :answer/id #uuid "cfc7ea99-dc34-5c5e-b665-c3586432a818" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.5" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b8532e0e-af6a-5a33-b916-4185a356c949" :answer/id #uuid "b8532e0e-af6a-5a33-b916-4185a356c949" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.75" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-29c9824b-2b87-54bb-a940-69ce3efe0d1b" :question/id #uuid "29c9824b-2b87-54bb-a940-69ce3efe0d1b" :question/math-academy-id "q-142904" :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X<2\,|\,Y=4) & =\frac{P((0\le X<2),Y=4)}{P(Y=4)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=0,Y=4)+P(X=1,Y=4)}{P(Y=4)} \\  & =\frac{f(0,4)+f(1,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(4) & =f(0,4)+f(1,4)+f(2,4) \\  & =0.05+0.1+0.05 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(0,4)=0.05$ and $f(1,4)=0.1.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X<2\,|\,Y=4) & =\frac{f(0,4)+f(1,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)} \\  & =\frac{0.05+0.1}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.15}{0.2} \\  & =0.75.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-78621176-1e00-508c-804a-571ad3daf5d2"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-78621176-1e00-508c-804a-571ad3daf5d2" :answer-field/id #uuid "78621176-1e00-508c-804a-571ad3daf5d2" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-10a5a9d4-3a44-5769-9f6b-52e2cb75f730" :answer-field/choices ["answer-c4a0b152-342f-53f4-afe1-60a1eb558763" "answer-bb32d8a6-9c26-5a27-9faa-26691c347856" "answer-4bcd313c-8a81-5a91-877f-2970fdc8ac87" "answer-2f47c227-7ea9-5c71-8c0a-c370a8c2740e" "answer-10a5a9d4-3a44-5769-9f6b-52e2cb75f730"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c4a0b152-342f-53f4-afe1-60a1eb558763" :answer/id #uuid "c4a0b152-342f-53f4-afe1-60a1eb558763" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.15" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bb32d8a6-9c26-5a27-9faa-26691c347856" :answer/id #uuid "bb32d8a6-9c26-5a27-9faa-26691c347856" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.25" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4bcd313c-8a81-5a91-877f-2970fdc8ac87" :answer/id #uuid "4bcd313c-8a81-5a91-877f-2970fdc8ac87" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.45" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2f47c227-7ea9-5c71-8c0a-c370a8c2740e" :answer/id #uuid "2f47c227-7ea9-5c71-8c0a-c370a8c2740e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.6" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-10a5a9d4-3a44-5769-9f6b-52e2cb75f730" :answer/id #uuid "10a5a9d4-3a44-5769-9f6b-52e2cb75f730" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.75" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-4ab049c7-8771-5b28-bd3b-011a826d75ca" :question/id #uuid "4ab049c7-8771-5b28-bd3b-011a826d75ca" :question/math-academy-id "q-142936" :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |

Find the conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)$ given that the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above." :question/worked-solution "The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the following set of conditional probabilities:

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=2)
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X=x\,|\,Y=2)=\frac{P(X=x,Y=2)}{P(Y=2)}=\frac{f(x,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.6$ | $0.4$ | $1$ |

Therefore, for $x\in \{0,2,4\},$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,|\,Y=2) & =\frac{f(0,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}=\frac{0.1}{0.4}=\frac{1}{4} \\ P(X=2\,|\,Y=2) & =\frac{f(2,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}=\frac{0.2}{0.4}=\frac{1}{2} \\ P(X=4\,|\,Y=2) & =\frac{f(4,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}=\frac{0.1}{0.4}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the conditional probability mass function can be represented by the following table:

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=P(Y=y\,|\,X=x).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the following set of conditional probabilities:

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,2)=P(Y=y\,|\,X=2)
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(Y=y\,|\,X=2)=\frac{P(X=2,Y=y)}{P(X=2)}=\frac{f(2,y)}{{f}_{X}(2)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=1$ | $0$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.6$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ | $0.4$ | $1$ |

Therefore, for $y\in \{0,1,2\},$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=0\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{f(2,0)}{{f}_{X}(2)}=\frac{0.1}{0.6}=\frac{1}{6} \\ P(Y=1\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{f(2,1)}{{f}_{X}(2)}=\frac{0.2}{0.6}=\frac{1}{3} \\ P(Y=2\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{f(2,2)}{{f}_{X}(2)}=\frac{0.3}{0.6}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- The **conditional probability mass function of $X$ given that $Y=y$,** denoted $f_{X|Y}(x|y),$ is defined as

$$
f_{X|Y}(x|y) = P(X = x \,|\, Y = y) = \dfrac{P(X = x, \, Y = y)}{P(Y=y)} = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y(y)},
$$

where  $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal mass function of $Y.$

- The **conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x,$** denoted $f_{Y|X}(y|x),$ is defined as

$$
f_{Y|X}(y|x) = P(Y = y \,|\, X = x) = \dfrac{P(X = x,\, Y = y)}{P(X=x)} = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)},
$$

where  $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal mass function of $X.$

**Watch out!** The conditional distribution of $X$ given $Y$ does *not* equal the conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$. That is, in general,

$$
f_{X|Y}(x|y)  \ne f_{Y|X}(y|x).
$$

Finally, if $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then 

$$
f_{X|Y}(x|y)=f_X(x),\qquad f_{Y|X}(y|x)=f_Y(y).
$$

In other words, if $X$  and  $Y$ are independent, then knowing the value of one random variable does not affect the probability distribution of the other." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186162164 :activity/expected-seconds 660.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}] "assertions" [[17592186161670 :question/problem "| ![](images/bc/bc562d54615dad55d095db2afed7626f62ff7ebf0ab6c5d45471b77ac30b6398.svg) | ![](images/5d/5dc49d43a26a7f7c244230d64b45a8f4347c9c0c9459c2e84d09c77bab196a6a.svg) | ![](images/3b/3b30c77d4719f1a02bb918bac935a9700f7895d4a08995493dca6a9707a59888.svg) | ![](images/0d/0d08226a482630bff20558817aceb35b7ba82c3f1b1cfe5143deb07deb8726f8.svg) |

$$
P(Y=0\,|\,X=3)=\frac{P(X=3,Y=0)}{P(X=3)}=\frac{f(3,0)}{{f}_{X}(3)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(3) & =f(3,0)+f(3,1)+f(3,2) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{2}{18}+\frac{2}{18}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{5}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

Compute $P(1<Y<7\,|\,X=2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above."] ["question-5f05ade6-f4a6-518d-b188-3b387ae00a2d" :question/worked-solution "By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<Y<7\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{P((1<Y<7),X=2)}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=2,(1<Y<7))}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=2,Y=3)+P(X=2,Y=5)}{P(X=2)} \\  & =\frac{f(2,3)+f(2,5)}{{f}_{X}(2)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(2) & =f(2,1)+f(2,3)+f(2,5)+f(2,7) \\  & =0+0.05+0.05+0.1 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(2,3)=0.05$ and $f(2,5)=0.05.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<Y<7\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{f(2,3)+f(2,5)}{{f}_{X}(2)} \\  & =\frac{0.05+0.05}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.1}{0.2} \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-5f05ade6-f4a6-518d-b188-3b387ae00a2d" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-28ba60db-712f-5d88-8bab-1c42ece049bb" :answer-field/id #uuid $$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X<2\,|\,Y=4) & =\frac{P((0\le X<2),Y=4)}{P(Y=4)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=0,Y=4)+P(X=1,Y=4)}{P(Y=4)} \\  & =\frac{f(0,4)+f(1,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(4) & =f(0,4)+f(1,4)+f(2,4) \\  & =0.05+0.1+0.05 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(0,4)=0.05$ and $f(1,4)=0.1.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X<2\,|\,Y=4) & =\frac{f(0,4)+f(1,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)} \\  & =\frac{0.05+0.1}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.15}{0.2} \\  & =0.75.\end{aligned}

Find the conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)$ given that the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above."] ["question-4ab049c7-8771-5b28-bd3b-011a826d75ca" :question/worked-solution "The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the following set of conditional probabilities:

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=2)
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X=x\,|\,Y=2)=\frac{P(X=x,Y=2)}{P(Y=2)}=\frac{f(x,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.6$ | $0.4$ | $1$ |

- The **conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x,$** denoted $f_{Y|X}(y|x),$ is defined as

$$
f_{Y|X}(y|x) = P(Y = y \,|\, X = x) = \dfrac{P(X = x,\, Y = y)}{P(X=x)} = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)},
$$

where  $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal mass function of $X.$

**Watch out!** The conditional distribution of $X$ given $Y$ does *not* equal the conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$. That is, in general,

$$
f_{X|Y}(x|y)  \ne f_{Y|X}(y|x).
$$

Finally, if $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then 

$$
f_{X|Y}(x|y)=f_X(x),\qquad f_{Y|X}(y|x)=f_Y(y).
$$

Conditional Probability"}] :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ |

Compute $P(Y=0 \,|\, X=1)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above." :question/worked-solution "By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required probability is given by

$$
P(Y = 0 \,|\, X = 1) = \dfrac{P(X = 1 , Y = 0)}{P(X = 1)} =  \dfrac{f(1,0)}{f_X(1)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(1) & =f(1,0)+f(1,1) \\  & =0.15+0.3 \\  & =0.45.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(1,0) = 0.15.$ 

Finally, substituting $f_X(1) = 0.45$ and $f(1,0) = 0.15$ in our formula above, we obtain

Round your answer to two decimal places." :question/worked-solution "By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<Y<3\,|\,X=0) & =\frac{P((0<Y<3),X=0)}{P(X=0)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=0,(0<Y<3))}{P(X=0)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=0,Y=1)+P(X=0,Y=2)}{P(X=0)} \\  & =\frac{f(0,1)+f(0,2)}{{f}_{X}(0)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(0) & =f(0,0)+f(0,1)+f(0,2)+f(0,3) \\  & =0.2+0+0.05+0.1 \\  & =0.35.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(0,1)=0$ and $f(0,2)=0.05.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into the formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<Y<3\,|\,X=0) & =\frac{f(0,1)+f(0,2)}{{f}_{X}(0)} \\  & =\frac{0+0.05}{0.35} \\  & =\frac{0.05}{0.35} \\  & ≈0.14.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186162318 :question/id #uuid "f8df4844-3002-5d2f-a7b0-d28f6004b192" :question/math-academy-id "q-114432"} {:db/id 17592186162377 :question/id #uuid "b9686b88-3d11-53fe-b55c-13e35af5fe85" :question/math-academy-id "q-142906"} {:db/id 17592186362880 :question/id #uuid "dcd58ecc-34a7-5fb8-abf6-ad622f5c0130" :question/math-academy-id "q-114434"} {:db/id 17592186363301 :question/id #uuid "747c65d8-31c2-5925-9aa8-b6c78ed4bae5" :question/math-academy-id "q-142899"} {:db/id 17592186363308 :question/id #uuid "aa531c7b-df4d-5520-9acf-a61999f53460" :question/math-academy-id "q-142901"} {:db/id 17592186363328 :question/id #uuid "e5d1e60b-f9aa-54a0-a39a-e6d8383bf77d" :question/math-academy-id "q-142907"} {:db/id 17592186410514 :question/id #uuid "b172bfa5-07a0-5df8-8d2d-99d558ae1db4" :question/math-academy-id "q-142896" :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1dea9c6c-8a37-5b15-a053-45fd4f8d2f9f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.6" :db/id 17592186410483} {:answer/id #uuid "c3b9f3ed-06e4-59ef-8471-d8398ce14731" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.25" :db/id 17592186410497} {:answer/id #uuid "d82990b6-7322-5310-a01d-936be990fc20" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.5" :db/id 17592186410501} {:answer/id #uuid "f4c7c149-9c87-52d8-aaf5-4888360f519e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.4" :db/id 17592186410504} {:answer/id #uuid "f7a8127b-532b-5c4e-95ea-e82e38e362d5" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.75" :db/id 17592186410505}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186410501} :answer-field/id #uuid "395c93a7-3493-526c-8001-2fe1cf196ffc" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186410507}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ |

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X\le 6\,|\,Y=3) & =\frac{P((0<X\le 6),Y=3)}{P(Y=3)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=3,Y=3)+P(X=6,Y=3)}{P(Y=3)} \\  & =\frac{f(3,3)+f(6,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(3) & =f(0,3)+f(3,3)+f(6,3)+f(9,3) \\  & =0+0.1+0+0.1 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(3,3)=0.1$ and $f(6,3)=0.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X\le 6\,|\,Y=3) & =\frac{f(3,3)+f(6,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)} \\  & =\frac{0.1+0}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.1}{0.2} \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186162104 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186161670 :question/id #uuid "2afabb9d-bd38-50f1-9afd-710ab839163c" :question/math-academy-id "e-10049"} :knowledge-point/id Find the conditional probability mass function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,3)$ given that the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above." :question/worked-solution "The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=P(Y=y\,|\,X=x).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the following set of conditional probabilities:

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,3)=P(Y=y\,|\,X=3)
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(Y=y\,|\,X=3)=\frac{P(X=3,Y=y)}{P(X=3)}=\frac{f(3,y)}{{f}_{X}(3)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ | $0.05$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.4$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.6$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.55$ | $0.3$ | $0.15$ | $1$ |

Therefore, for $y\in {1,2,3},$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=1\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{f(3,1)}{{f}_{X}(3)}=\frac{0.4}{0.6}=\frac{2}{3} \\ P(Y=2\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{f(3,2)}{{f}_{X}(3)}=\frac{0.1}{0.6}=\frac{1}{6} \\ P(Y=3\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{f(3,3)}{{f}_{X}(3)}=\frac{0.1}{0.6}=\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the conditional probability mass function can be represented by the following table:   

| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,3)$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ |"} {:db/id 17592186410513 :question/id #uuid "9f027a74-2cf2-5941-ad79-db682e13a988" :question/math-academy-id "q-142945" :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "0edd7b5b-c6e3-57a4-8be5-217568bb3909" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=y).
$$

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,4)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=4)
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X=x\,|\,Y=4)=\frac{P(X=x,Y=4)}{P(Y=4)}=\frac{f(x,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |

| $X=1$ | $0.15$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ | $0.55$ |

| $X=3$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.2$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.2$ | $0.6$ | $0.2$ | $1$ |

Therefore, for $x\in {1,2,3},$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,|\,Y=4) & =\frac{f(1,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)}=\frac{0.1}{0.2}=\frac{1}{2} \\ P(X=2\,|\,Y=4) & =\frac{f(2,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)}=\frac{0.05}{0.2}=\frac{1}{4} \\ P(X=3\,|\,Y=4) & =\frac{f(3,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)}=\frac{0.05}{0.2}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the conditional probability mass function can be represented by the following table:   

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |

Compute $f_{X|Y}(2 \,|\, 2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above." :question/worked-solution "The conditional probability mass function $f_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
f_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) = P(X = x \,|\, Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability

$$
f_{X|Y}(2 \,|\, 2) = P(X = 2 \,|\, Y = 2).
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X = 2 \,|\, Y = 2) = \dfrac{P(X = 2, Y = 2)}{P(Y = 2)} = \dfrac{f(2,2)}{f_Y(2)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(2) & =f(1,2)+f(2,2)+f(3,2) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{7}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, $f(2,2) = \dfrac{1}{6}.$ 

Finally, substituting  $f_Y(2) = \dfrac{7}{18}$ and $f(2,2) = \dfrac{1}{6}$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(2\,|\,2) & =P(X=2\,|\,Y=2) \\  & =\frac{f(2,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{6})}{(\frac{7}{18})} \\  & =\frac{3}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186162316 :question/id #uuid "e4cfc159-d36d-5d4f-9156-02dbd7e02b7b" :question/math-academy-id "q-114424"} {:db/id 17592186162373 :question/id #uuid "decec22b-76b8-53c1-a1aa-2d4890c3f678" :question/math-academy-id "q-142549"} {:db/id 17592186363280 :question/id #uuid "e911b538-24df-51a8-a134-2c4a130edca5" :question/math-academy-id "q-142890" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186162105 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "277b8807-fb74-5ad3-a89b-92dbf90bc075" :knowledge-point/title "Computing the Value of a Conditional Probability Mass Function at a Point"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "772f1af4-3e1a-5d24-b6f2-84e08728280e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0.33" :db/id 17592186363282} {:answer/id #uuid "ed679624-c3a1-592b-b00b-85dbdf0ab4f4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0.27" :db/id 17592186363283} {:answer/id #uuid "65636e3f-fc1c-570a-afb9-b6e83ab76155" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0.67" :db/id 17592186363284} {:answer/id #uuid "145ae614-6fb3-5df0-adc4-a7a23c2f414d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0.19" :db/id 17592186363285} {:answer/id #uuid "e6479b1c-edbb-5852-9f86-63ee058f8c17" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0.41" :db/id 17592186363286}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "ed679624-c3a1-592b-b00b-85dbdf0ab4f4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0.27" :db/id 17592186363283} :answer-field/id #uuid "945c9fdc-f2f4-578d-8093-3c96735abd64" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186363281}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485 :db/ident :question.difficulty/easy} :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |

Round your answer to $2$ decimal places." :question/worked-solution "The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(4\,|\,2)=P(X=4\,|\,Y=2).
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X=4\,|\,Y=2)=\frac{P(X=4,Y=2)}{P(Y=2)}=\frac{f(4,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(2) & =f(2,2)+f(4,2) \\  & =0.4+0.15 \\  & =0.55.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, $f(4,2)=0.15.$ 

Finally, substituting  ${f}_{Y}(2)=0.55$ and $f(4,2)=0.15$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(4\,|\,2) & =P(X=4\,|\,Y=2) \\  & =\frac{f(4,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)} \\  & =\frac{0.15}{0.55} \\  & ≈0.27.\end{aligned}

- The **conditional probability mass function of $X$ given that $Y=y$,** denoted $f_{X|Y}(x|y),$ is defined as $$f_{X|Y}(x|y) = P(X = x \,|\, Y = y) = \dfrac{P(X = x, \, Y = y)}{P(Y=y)} = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y(y)},$$ where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal mass function of $Y.$

- The **conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x,$** denoted $f_{Y|X}(y|x),$ is defined as $$f_{Y|X}(y|x) = P(Y = y \,|\, X = x) = \dfrac{P(X = x,\, Y = y)}{P(X=x)} = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)},$$ where $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal mass function of $X.$

**Watch out!** The conditional distribution of $X$ given $Y$ does *not* equal the conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$. That is, in general,

$$f_{X|Y}(x|y) \ne f_{Y|X}(y|x).$$

Finally, if $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then

$$f_{X|Y}(x|y)=f_X(x),\qquad f_{Y|X}(y|x)=f_Y(y).$$

In other words, if $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then knowing the value of one random variable does not affect the probability distribution of the other." :tutorial/id #uuid "1cbdc2c5-105c-5f9a-b4f4-7e4651bdc789" :tutorial/math-academy-id 6273 :tutorial/title "Conditional Probability Mass Functions"} :step/id #uuid "acc71c94-7794-57f0-bfff-16c3d8ed9e31" :step/math-academy-id 38019 :step/next {:db/id 17592186163066}}] :activity/title "Conditional Distributions for Discrete Random Variables" :activity/type {:db/id 17592186045463 :db/ident :activity.type/lesson} :db/id 17592186162164} {:db/id 17592186163004 :step/content {:db/id 17592186163288 :tutorial/content "Let's recall the multiplication law for conditional probability for two events ![](images/32/3207697e43e4f88223ad85c16964c3103a50c0c999a4ca14417695158d45526b.svg) and ![](images/5d/5d8b650b90c85fbc0db5e4b6fae61767e293a843d18a2526f3ee4157733e1f4b.svg) ![](images/44/44229a2a35108e36c1348009a552be50e798af9b2807f49c4e4ef8515ed7eefe.svg)

In other words, if $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then knowing the value of one random variable does not affect the probability distribution of the other." :tutorial/id #uuid "1cbdc2c5-105c-5f9a-b4f4-7e4651bdc789" :tutorial/math-academy-id 6273 :tutorial/title "Conditional Probability Mass Functions"} :step/id #uuid "acc71c94-7794-57f0-bfff-16c3d8ed9e31" :step/math-academy-id 38019 :step/next {:db/id 17592186163066}} {:db/id 17592186163065 :step/content {:db/id 17592186162104 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186161670 :question/id #uuid "2afabb9d-bd38-50f1-9afd-710ab839163c" :question/math-academy-id "e-10049"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "ebabf742-2b8d-5392-a077-f34e8f4bd034" :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186162317} {:db/id 17592186162374} {:db/id 17592186272384} {:db/id 17592186363335} {:db/id 17592186363342} {:db/id 17592186363349} {:db/id 17592186400965} {:db/id 17592186400972} {:db/id 17592186410511} {:db/id 17592186410513}] :knowledge-point/title "Computing a Conditional Probability Mass Function"} :step/id #uuid "000582c8-50ec-5bfc-b34a-c1cec0a03e2c" :step/math-academy-id 37921} {:db/id 17592186163066 :step/content {:db/id 17592186162105 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186161671 :question/id #uuid "0e42cf0f-f1bd-5762-a4fc-3cedec697c14" :question/math-academy-id "e-10050"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "277b8807-fb74-5ad3-a89b-92dbf90bc075" :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186162316} {:db/id 17592186162373} {:db/id 17592186363280} {:db/id 17592186363287} {:db/id 17592186363294} {:db/id 17592186363315} {:db/id 17592186410512} {:db/id 17592186410515}] :knowledge-point/title "Computing the Value of a Conditional Probability Mass Function at a Point"} :step/id #uuid "f16763f3-a2e5-5d38-9f53-ce65ea110dc5" :step/math-academy-id 37922 :step/next {:db/id 17592186163065}} {:db/id 17592186163325 :tutorial/content "We can now define two more probability mass functions as follows:

- The **conditional probability mass function of $X$ given that $Y=y$,** denoted $f_{X|Y}(x|y),$ is defined as $$f_{X|Y}(x|y) = P(X = x \,|\, Y = y) = \dfrac{P(X = x, \, Y = y)}{P(Y=y)} = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y(y)},$$ where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal mass function of $Y.$

- The **conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x,$** denoted $f_{Y|X}(y|x),$ is defined as $$f_{Y|X}(y|x) = P(Y = y \,|\, X = x) = \dfrac{P(X = x,\, Y = y)}{P(X=x)} = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)},$$ where $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal mass function of $X.$

**Watch out!** The conditional distribution of $X$ given $Y$ does *not* equal the conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$. That is, in general,

$$f_{X|Y}(x|y) \ne f_{Y|X}(y|x).$$

Finally, if $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then

$$f_{X|Y}(x|y)=f_X(x),\qquad f_{Y|X}(y|x)=f_Y(y).$$

In other words, if $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then knowing the value of one random variable does not affect the probability distribution of the other." :tutorial/id #uuid "1cbdc2c5-105c-5f9a-b4f4-7e4651bdc789" :tutorial/math-academy-id 6273 :tutorial/title "Conditional Probability Mass Functions"} {:db/id 17592186045463 :db/ident :activity.type/lesson} {:activity/course {:db/id 17592186046659} :activity/first-step {:db/id 17592186410519} :activity/id #uuid "4f58fa0a-3eab-578c-8ede-b29945f6d461" :activity/scope {:db/id 17592186049149 :topic/id #uuid "de945224-de03-5292-84ca-39d9ddf3f7e4" :topic/math-academy-id 3003} :activity/steps [{:db/id 17592186410516 :step/content {:db/id 17592186410515 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "36eae30e-fa0d-5135-a62d-0465c3393122" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186410485} {:answer/id #uuid "500b7039-9773-5a4d-a57b-2ec78d1c6cc4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3}{13}" :db/id 17592186410489} {:answer/id #uuid "568228f9-502e-5052-aae6-cf24f3f3e87c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{7}{16}" :db/id 17592186410490} {:answer/id #uuid "7f2cbc96-2672-5c50-abb6-ff77349a1002" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}" :db/id 17592186410495} {:answer/id #uuid "b71aacf7-31c6-5c18-bf8d-c7c655c001fb" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{5}{13}" :db/id 17592186410496}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186410489} :answer-field/id #uuid "b9630d02-fcc6-50aa-af4a-264fb35a6574" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186410509}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "b1e5d993-4954-596b-9a63-c575f6c7babb" :question/math-academy-id "q-142903" :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=P(Y=y\,|\,X=x).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(3\,|\,3)=P(Y=3\,|\,X=3).
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(Y=3\,|\,X=3)=\frac{P(X=3,Y=3)}{P(X=3)}=\frac{f(3,3)}{{f}_{X}(3)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(3) & =f(3,1)+f(3,2)+f(3,3) \\  & =\frac{5}{32}+\frac{5}{32}+\frac{3}{32} \\  & =\frac{13}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, $f(3,3)=\frac{3}{32}.$ 

Finally, substituting  ${f}_{X}(3)=\frac{13}{32}$ and $f(3,3)=\frac{3}{32}$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y|X}(3\,|\,3) & =P(Y=3\,|\,X=3) \\  & =\frac{f(3,3)}{{f}_{X}(3)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{32})}{(\frac{13}{32})} \\  & =\frac{3}{13}.\end{aligned}

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=P(Y=y\,|\,X=x).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the following set of conditional probabilities:

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,3)=P(Y=y\,|\,X=3)
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(Y=y\,|\,X=3)=\frac{P(X=3,Y=y)}{P(X=3)}=\frac{f(3,y)}{{f}_{X}(3)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ | $0.05$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.4$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.6$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.55$ | $0.3$ | $0.15$ | $1$ |

Therefore, for $y\in {1,2,3},$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=1\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{f(3,1)}{{f}_{X}(3)}=\frac{0.4}{0.6}=\frac{2}{3} \\ P(Y=2\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{f(3,2)}{{f}_{X}(3)}=\frac{0.1}{0.6}=\frac{1}{6} \\ P(Y=3\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{f(3,3)}{{f}_{X}(3)}=\frac{0.1}{0.6}=\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the conditional probability mass function can be represented by the following table:   

| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,3)$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ |"} :step/id #uuid "30942c86-dbc3-5faa-928f-8a3e27c6ef2a" :step/next {:db/id 17592186410520}} {:db/id 17592186410518 :step/content {:db/id 17592186410514 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1dea9c6c-8a37-5b15-a053-45fd4f8d2f9f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.6" :db/id 17592186410483} {:answer/id #uuid "c3b9f3ed-06e4-59ef-8471-d8398ce14731" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.25" :db/id 17592186410497} {:answer/id #uuid "d82990b6-7322-5310-a01d-936be990fc20" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.5" :db/id 17592186410501} {:answer/id #uuid "f4c7c149-9c87-52d8-aaf5-4888360f519e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.4" :db/id 17592186410504} {:answer/id #uuid "f7a8127b-532b-5c4e-95ea-e82e38e362d5" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.75" :db/id 17592186410505}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186410501} :answer-field/id #uuid "395c93a7-3493-526c-8001-2fe1cf196ffc" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186410507}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "b172bfa5-07a0-5df8-8d2d-99d558ae1db4" :question/math-academy-id "q-142896" :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ |

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X\le 6\,|\,Y=3) & =\frac{P((0<X\le 6),Y=3)}{P(Y=3)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=3,Y=3)+P(X=6,Y=3)}{P(Y=3)} \\  & =\frac{f(3,3)+f(6,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(3) & =f(0,3)+f(3,3)+f(6,3)+f(9,3) \\  & =0+0.1+0+0.1 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(3,3)=0.1$ and $f(6,3)=0.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X\le 6\,|\,Y=3) & =\frac{f(3,3)+f(6,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)} \\  & =\frac{0.1+0}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.1}{0.2} \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "b0812b16-60e1-5ebb-80af-c271cd3f189c" :step/next {:db/id 17592186410516}} {:db/id 17592186410519 :step/content {:db/id 17592186410512 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "4176ad50-617b-5bbe-9749-530c4518c952" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.50" :db/id 17592186410486} {:answer/id #uuid "461964e4-b6e1-5a7d-85c6-1b999a2b0407" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.37" :db/id 17592186410487} {:answer/id #uuid "4deb08c4-9a80-57d4-8a91-17d29d971092" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.18" :db/id 17592186410488} {:answer/id #uuid "cb1bcdc1-72d1-5f68-bb9d-cd8c02cd1c36" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.42" :db/id 17592186410498} {:answer/id #uuid "d1106665-3f25-50f6-bf70-205dfb7d3993" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0.13" :db/id 17592186410499}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186410498} :answer-field/id #uuid "38673cd4-d233-5042-adf0-a6d70114ec93" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186410506}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "70462da6-df40-572c-b721-518f7d0fb229" :question/math-academy-id "q-142893" :question/problem "| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |

$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

17592186045417] [17592186046658 1005 17592186046975 17592186045417] [17592186046658 1007 "Mathematics for Machine Learning" 17592186045417] [17592186046658 1008 "Our Mathematics for Machine Learning course provides a comprehensive foundation of the essential mathematical tools required to study modern machine learning.
This course is divided into three main categories: linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and probability & statistics. The linear algebra section covers crucial machine learning fundamentals such as matrices, vector spaces, diagonalization, projections, singular value decomposition, and regression, as well as dimensionality reduction techniques such as principal component analysis. The multivariable calculus section develops the tools needed for optimization and learning algorithms, including vector and matrix calculus. Finally, the probability and statistics section covers random variables, point estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, and confidence intervals.
On completing this course, students will be well-prepared for a university-level machine learning course that tackles concepts such as gradient descent, neural networks, backpropagation, support vector machines, naive Bayes classifiers, and Gaussian mixture models." 17592186045417] [17592186046658 1009 "The course begins with foundational topics in set theory and logic. Students develop a precise mathematical language for describing sets, functions, and predicates, and are introduced to key ideas such as supremum and infimum, as well as argmax and argmin notation. Logical reasoning and Boolean functions are also studied, providing important conceptual motivation for understanding the expressive limitations of some simple machine learning models, such as why certain functions (e.g. XOR) cannot be represented by a single-layer neural network.
Students then explore matrices in-depth. They study Gaussian elimination, solve systems of equations, learn about determinants and their properties, and compute inverse matrices. These tools form the computational backbone of many machine learning algorithms.
As part of this course, students perform a deep dive into vector spaces, exploring linear independence, subspaces, bases, dimension, rank, and nullity. They also study operations such as the Hadamard product, which appears naturally in element-wise computations in neural networks. Students generalize key concepts to abstract vector spaces and inner product spaces, and study orthogonality, projections, and the Gram–Schmidt process.
Students will learn how to find eigenvectors of a matrix, compute matrix diagonalizations, and extend these ideas to orthogonal diagonalization of symmetric matrices. These techniques underpin dimensionality reduction methods and are central to understanding the structure of data.
The course then develops key applications of linear algebra in machine learning. Students study singular value decomposition and its relationship to principal component analysis, and learn how these tools are used for dimensionality reduction, feature extraction, and identifying structure in high-dimensional datasets. Linear least-squares problems and regression techniques are also studied as foundational methods for fitting models to data.
A solid grasp of multivariable calculus is essential for understanding modern machine learning algorithms. In this course, students become well-versed in partial derivatives and gradient vectors (used in gradient-based optimization), the multivariable chain rule (essential for backpropagation), and vector-valued functions. Students extend differentiation to maps between multi-dimensional vector spaces and develop the tools of vector and matrix calculus used to compute gradients of loss functions in neural networks.
Students also study optimization of multivariable functions, including critical points, second derivative tests, and constrained optimization using Lagrange multipliers. These techniques form the mathematical foundation of algorithms such as support vector machines and constrained optimization problems in machine learning.
Students work with standard multivariable surfaces to build intuition for loss surfaces, and study double integrals as a tool for understanding continuous probability distributions.
On the probability and statistics side, students study discrete and continuous random variables, including probability density functions, cumulative distribution functions, transformations, expectation, moments, variance, and Bayes' theorem. Important probability distributions are explored in detail.
Students extend their understanding to joint, marginal, and conditional distributions, as well as sums and products of random variables. Topics such as covariance, correlation, and multivariate normal distributions are introduced, which are essential in probabilistic modeling.
The course concludes with parametric inference, focusing on point estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, and confidence intervals, which form the statistical foundation for many machine learning 17592186046982 17592186045417] [17592186046659 1007 "Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences I" 17592186045417] [17592186046659 1008 "Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences I develops the core mathematical structures and analytical tools used throughout theoretical and applied physics. Building on calculus and introductory linear algebra, the course introduces vector geometry, multivariable analysis, and differential equations in a unified framework designed for modeling physical systems.
